scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: The Daniel Asia papers contain manuscripts, scores and sketches of Asia's compositions, including symphonies and orchestral works; chamber works; cello and piano concertos, as well as other piano and solo instrumental compositions; song cycles and choral works and corresponding orchestral arrangements; and Asia's opera Tin Angel . The papers also include correspondence relating to fundraising, programming, recording, and commissions; photographic prints and negatives including headshots, publicity photos, performance and rehearsal photos, professional and family gatherings, and candid snapshots; assorted professional files, reviews, publicity, and programs; and a series dedicated to Musical Elements, Asia's contemporary chamber ensemble, which he co-directs with composer Robert Beaser.

arrangement.head: Arrangement
arrangement.p: The collection is arranged into 7 series as follows: Series I. Music (arranged in sub-series by composition type); Series II. Reviews and Publicity; Series III. Programs; Series IV. Musical Elements (this series consists of materials relating to Asia's chamber ensemble of that name, and is arranged into sub-series similar to those of the broader collection, with the exception of Photographs, which have been included in Series VI); Series V. Correspondence (arranged alphabetically by name or organizatoin); Series VI. Photographs; Series VII. Files (arranged by file category).

accessrestrict.head: Conditions Governing Access
accessrestrict.p: The collection is open for research.

prefercite.head: Preferred Citation
prefercite.p: MSS 91, Daniel Asia Papers in the Irving S. Gilmore Music Library of Yale University.

userestrict.head: Conditions Governing Use
userestrict.p: The Daniel Asia Papers are the physical property of the Irving S. Gilmore Music Library of Yale University. Copyrights belong to the composers and authors, or their legal heirs and assigns.

processinfo.head: Processing Information
processinfo.p: Some series are not processed to the fullest level. Series II. Programs and Series III. Reviews and Publicity are minimally processed; Series VII. Files are arranged by type of file and minimally processed.
